author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Alpha School is opening three Greater Boston locations this fall, bringing an artificial-intelligence-centered private-school model to Lexington, Beacon Hill and Jamaica Plain. The Jamaica Plain campus will occupy the former Croft School site. Tuition is $65,000 a year, and the network says the three campuses can eventually serve about 500 students from kindergarten through eighth grade.

The school says personalized software assesses each child’s academic level and lets students complete core subjects in roughly two hours a day. Adults in the classrooms are called guides and focus on motivation and emotional support; Alpha says those positions pay at least $100,000. The remainder of the school day is organized around workshops in entrepreneurship, financial literacy, public speaking and other practical skills.

The model is also prompting scrutiny. MIT education-technology researcher Justin Reich told NBC10 Boston that individualized computer work can reduce opportunities for students to deliberate and learn alongside classmates with different perspectives. Alpha argues that shorter academic blocks leave more time for human connection and applied learning. The openings will give Massachusetts families and educators a local test of those competing claims as enrollment builds over several years.
dek: The private K-8 network is bringing its two-hour personalized-academics model to Lexington, Beacon Hill and Jamaica Plain at $65,000 a year.
headline: AI-focused Alpha School opens three Greater Boston campuses
